+# Cover archival
+
+Cover IDs are written as ten decimal digits. The first four digits are the
+archive.org item ID (one million covers), the next two are the batch ID
+(10,000 covers), and the last four identify the cover in its batch. For example,
+cover `8819999` is `0008819999`, item `0008`, batch `81`.
+
+Each batch has four uncompressed zip files, one per size. They are staged at
+`<data_root>/items/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>_<batch_id>.zip`.
+`size_prefix` is empty for originals and `s_`, `m_`, or `l_` for thumbnails.
+Entries are `<10-digit-id>.jpg` or `<10-digit-id>-S.jpg`, `-M.jpg`, `-L.jpg`.
+For example, the medium cover above is in
+`items/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_81.zip` as `0008819999-M.jpg`.
+The matching archive.org download URL is
+`https://archive.org/download/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_81.zip/0008819999-M.jpg`.
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. Configure coverstore, then call `archive.archive(test=False)` to stage local
+   files in zips. This selects at most 10,000 unarchived, non-failed rows per
+   call. Missing local images are marked `failed=true`. Staged rows have
+   `archived=true`, `uploaded=false`, and filenames pointing into local zips.
+2. For each staged item and batch, call
+   `archive.Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True)`.
+   The uploader checks all four zip files on archive.org before finalization.
+   If verification fails, staged zips remain on disk and `uploaded` stays false.
+3. Finalization changes all four filename fields to direct download URLs, sets
+   `uploaded=true`, and removes the staged zips. Batch lock files remain in the
+   item directory to coordinate concurrent runs. A failed upload can be retried.
+
+Legacy tar and index entries remain readable through the existing coverstore
+reader. They are no longer generated. Database `uploaded` is the authority for
+remote retrieval of newly archived covers; no cover ID range is hard-coded for
+remote redirects.

+# Cover archival
+
+Cover IDs are written as ten decimal digits. The first four digits are the
+archive.org item ID (one million covers), the next two are the batch ID
+(10,000 covers), and the last four identify the cover in its batch. For example,
+cover `8819999` is `0008819999`, item `0008`, batch `81`.
+
+Each batch has four uncompressed zip files, one per size. They are staged at
+`<data_root>/items/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>_<batch_id>.zip`.
+`size_prefix` is empty for originals and `s_`, `m_`, or `l_` for thumbnails.
+Entries are `<10-digit-id>.jpg` or `<10-digit-id>-S.jpg`, `-M.jpg`, `-L.jpg`.
+For example, the medium cover above is in
+`items/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_81.zip` as `0008819999-M.jpg`.
+The matching archive.org download URL is
+`https://archive.org/download/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_81.zip/0008819999-M.jpg`.
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. Configure coverstore, then call `archive.archive(test=False)` to stage local
+   files in zips. This selects at most 10,000 unarchived, non-failed rows per
+   call. Missing local images are marked `failed=true`. Staged rows have
+   `archived=true`, `uploaded=false`, and filenames pointing into local zips.
+2. For each staged item and batch, call
+   `archive.Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True)`.
+   The uploader checks all four zip files on archive.org before finalization.
+   If verification fails, staged zips remain on disk and `uploaded` stays false.
+3. Finalization changes all four filename fields to direct download URLs, sets
+   `uploaded=true`, and removes the staged zips. Batch lock files remain in the
+   item directory to coordinate concurrent runs. A failed upload can be retried.
+
+Legacy tar and index entries remain readable through the existing coverstore
+reader. They are no longer generated. Database `uploaded` is the authority for
+remote retrieval of newly archived covers; no cover ID range is hard-coded for
+remote redirects.
